items.title: Topological defect insertion in a specified model
items.design_state: Assigned A-page definition authored from the exact future item contract.
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and a smooth $d$-manifold $M$, possibly with boundary. Fix the metric and signature, orientation and any time orientation, the geometric background bundles or lifts required by the model, and the boundary conditions. A **selected model** $\mathcal T$ on $M$ consists of a specified configuration space $\mathcal C_{\mathcal T}(M)$ of fields, including each field bundle, regularity class, and admissible boundary behavior; a specified collection of local observables and their supports; a set $\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}$ of admissible finite observable lists with boundary data; a declared value space $\mathcal V_{\mathcal T}$ (for example, $\mathbb C$ or a specified distribution space); and a normalized correlation functional $C_{\mathcal T}:\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}\to\mathcal V_{\mathcal T}$. The model also fixes its unit system, action and charge normalizations, and any regulator, measure, or renormalization prescription used to define $C_{\mathcal T}$. These are model inputs: this definition does not construct them or assume a general interacting continuum theory exists.

A **defect insertion** in $\mathcal T$ is data $(j,\lambda)$ where $j:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M^\circ$ is a smooth embedding of a manifold $\Sigma$ without boundary whose image is closed in the interior $M^\circ=M\setminus\partial M$, and $\lambda$ is the model-specified local field, operator, or boundary-condition data supported on $j(\Sigma)$. Its codimension is $d-\dim\Sigma$. The model must define the modified correlator $C_{\mathcal T}(D_{j,\lambda};O_1,\ldots,O_n)$ for every allowed list of other insertions $O_j$. An orientation, coorientation, or framing is included in $\lambda$ whenever the model needs it. A defect network is a finite list of such strata with a specified incidence relation; each allowed meeting stratum has a stated order of incident labels and a local junction operator inserted by the model. A list of strata or a picture without this field and junction data is not a defect insertion.

An **isotopy** of this insertion is a smooth family of embeddings $j_t:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M^\circ$, $t\in[0,1]$, that transports all included orientation, coorientation, framing, and junction data, leaves the boundary conditions fixed, and keeps every support disjoint from every other insertion throughout the deformation. The insertion is **topological in $\mathcal T$** if, for every admissible list of other insertions and boundary data and every such isotopy, the model-defined correlators satisfy

$$C_{\mathcal T}(D_{j_0,\lambda_0};O_1,\ldots,O_n)=C_{\mathcal T}(D_{j_1,\lambda_1};O_1,\ldots,O_n).$$

This is a property to verify for the specified model and insertion, not an automatic consequence of assigning a defect label or drawing a crossing. No physical quantity with units is introduced here; all dimensional quantities and normalizations remain those declared by $\mathcal T$.
items.physical_scope: A definition for a named field-theory or quantum model whose admissible configurations and correlation functionals are specified; it asserts neither existence of a general continuum QFT nor realization of any proposed defect.

references.title: Davide Gaiotto, Anton Kapustin, Nathan Seiberg, and Brian Willett, Generalized Global Symmetries
references.locator: §1 Introduction, PDF pp. 1–3, especially equations (1.1)–(1.2): codimension-(q+1) operator support, correlation-function invariance under deformation, and group fusion.

references.title: Nils Carqueville, Lecture Notes on 2-Dimensional Defect TQFT
references.locator: §2.1, PDF pp. 5–8: oriented defect bordisms, region and defect labels, isotopy classes, and the functorial correlator assignment in the explicitly two-dimensional TQFT setting.

items.title: Topological interface between specified models
items.design_state: Assigned A-page definition authored from the exact future item contract.
items.statement:
Use the selected-model and defect-insertion data from the preceding defect definition: a model specifies its manifold, background and boundary data, fields with regularity conditions, unit conventions, and correlator functional; an insertion is a model-defined local modification supported on an embedded submanifold. Let $\mathcal T_-$ and $\mathcal T_+$ be two such models in the same spacetime dimension $d$ on the same smooth manifold $M$. Their metric or signature, background bundles, boundary conditions, field normalizations, and units must either agree or be related by an explicitly supplied identification. No such identification is inferred from names or equal dimensions.

A **codimension-one interface** from $\mathcal T_-$ to $\mathcal T_+$ is data $(\mathcal W,\mathcal I)$ where $\mathcal W\hookrightarrow M^\circ$ is a closed smooth embedded hypersurface with a chosen coorientation and a specified collar $\mathcal W\times(-\epsilon,\epsilon)$, $\epsilon>0$. The negative side uses $\mathcal T_-$ and the positive side uses $\mathcal T_+$. The interface data $\mathcal I$ is a specified local transmission condition, operator map, or boundary condition relating the one-sided field data in that collar, together with any orientation, framing, or junction labels required by the models. The combined model must assign a correlator $C_{\mathcal T_-,\mathcal T_+}(\mathcal I(\mathcal W);O_1,\ldots,O_n)$ to every stated admissible list of insertions. The interface is **topological** when this correlator obeys the isotopy-invariance criterion of the preceding defect definition, with the two side labels and all interface data transported and no other insertion crossed.

For interfaces $\mathcal I_{01}:\mathcal T_0\to\mathcal T_1$ and $\mathcal I_{12}:\mathcal T_1\to\mathcal T_2$, define their **fusion** only when the model supplies a product collar containing two parallel interfaces at separation $\delta>0$ and, as $\delta\downarrow0$, every declared correlator with the pair converges to the correlator of a single interface. The limiting insertion, its normalization, and its junction data are the fused interface $\mathcal I_{12}\star\mathcal I_{01}:\mathcal T_0\to\mathcal T_2$. If this limit is not part of the model or does not exist, no single fused interface is asserted.

An **endodefect** has $\mathcal T_- = \mathcal T_+$ as the same complete model data, not merely models with similarly named fields. The **transparent identity interface** $\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}$ is the model-supplied transmission condition that identifies the two sides without changing any correlator. An endodefect is an **invertible symmetry interface** only if a two-sided inverse exists under the stated fusion operation, both composites equal $\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}$ in all declared correlators, and the induced map is an automorphism of the model's observable and background data preserving its correlators. A topological interface between distinct source and target models is an interface, not an internal symmetry of either model. No supersymmetry or BPS condition is implicit; claiming one requires additional model data and a separate check of the specified supercharges and their domains.

No dimensional quantity is added by this definition. Each model and interface must retain its declared unit system and normalization, and this definition does not assert that a continuum fusion limit exists.
items.physical_scope: A definition of a codimension-one interface for named models with compatible spacetime, background, boundary, and unit data; it assumes only model-defined correlators and a stated fusion limit, and asserts no general continuum interface exists.

references.title: Davide Gaiotto, Anton Kapustin, Nathan Seiberg, and Brian Willett, Generalized Global Symmetries
references.locator: §1 Introduction, PDF pp. 1–3: topological defect operators and their group-like fusion when they implement an ordinary or higher-form symmetry.

references.title: Nils Carqueville, Lecture Notes on 2-Dimensional Defect TQFT
references.locator: §2.1, PDF pp. 5–8: labeled regions, source/target maps on domain walls, isotopy classes of defect bordisms, and functorial correlators in oriented 2D TQFT.

items.title: A nontrivial Z2 topological defect in finite quantum mechanics
items.design_state: Owner-directed B-page finite-model example or counterexample, proved locally; no empirical or continuum claim.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$ with its standard positive inner product, and let the Hamiltonian be the zero matrix $H=0$. This defines a finite-dimensional $0+1$-dimensional quantum-mechanical transfer model: propagation through an interval of length $s\ge0$ is $e^{-sH}=I$, where $s$ is Euclidean time in units with $\hbar=1$. The local observables are all matrices in $\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H)$, and a correlator with fixed boundary vectors is the matrix element of their time-ordered product with the propagation matrices between insertions.

Let $G=\mathbb Z_2=\{0,1\}$ with addition modulo $2$, and define $U_0=I$ and $U_1=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Insert $U_g$ at an interior point $\tau\in(0,T)$ of the time interval $[0,T]$. For any finite ordered list of other fixed observable insertions, moving $\tau$ within a gap that contains no other insertion leaves their order relative to $U_g$ unchanged. The insertion is a nontrivial invertible $\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry defect of this model.
items.physical_scope: An exact finite-dimensional 0+1-dimensional quantum-mechanical transfer model with hbar=1 and zero Hamiltonian; no continuum QFT or empirical claim is made.

references.title: Davide Gaiotto, Anton Kapustin, Nathan Seiberg, and Brian Willett, Generalized Global Symmetries
references.locator: §1 Introduction, PDF pp. 1–3: a symmetry defect is a topological operator with group-like fusion; the finite matrix representation and verification here are local.

references.title: Nils Carqueville, Lecture Notes on 2-Dimensional Defect TQFT
references.locator: §2.1, PDF pp. 5–8: model-defined defect insertions and isotopy classes; this example is 0+1-dimensional and is checked directly.

items.title: An invertible interface between two finite quantum-mechanical models
items.design_state: Owner-directed B-page finite-model example or counterexample, proved locally; no empirical or continuum claim.
items.statement:
Use natural units $\hbar=1$. Let the source model $\mathcal T_-$ and target model $\mathcal T_+$ each have Hilbert space $\mathbb C^2$ with its standard positive inner product and all complex $2\times2$ matrices as local observables. Their Hamiltonian matrices are

$$H_- = \begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&\Delta\end{pmatrix},\qquad H_+ = \begin{pmatrix}\Delta&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \Delta>0.$$

Here $\Delta$ has units of energy and a Euclidean time interval $s$ has units of inverse energy; propagation is $e^{-sH_\pm}$. Define the interface map

$$V=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}:\mathcal H_-\longrightarrow\mathcal H_+.$$

The target observable corresponding to $O_-\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^2)$ is $O_+=VO_-V^\dagger$. For a single interface at time $\tau\in(0,T)$, its transfer amplitude between boundary vectors $\psi_-\in\mathcal H_-$ and $\psi_+\in\mathcal H_+$ is

$$C_\tau=\langle\psi_+,e^{-(T-\tau)H_+}V e^{-\tau H_-}\psi_-\rangle.$$

This is an invertible topological interface between two specified models. It is an internal symmetry only if the source and target models are subsequently identified as one complete model.
items.physical_scope: An exact finite-dimensional 0+1-dimensional quantum-mechanical interface with hbar=1 and positive energy gap Delta; no continuum QFT or empirical claim is made.

references.title: Nils Carqueville, Lecture Notes on 2-Dimensional Defect TQFT
references.locator: §2.1, PDF pp. 5–8: source and target region labels for a defect wall and model-defined correlators; the finite-dimensional matrix example is verified locally.

items.title: A topological interface between different models is not an internal symmetry
items.design_state: Owner-directed B-page finite-model example or counterexample, proved locally; no empirical or continuum claim.
items.statement: Every topological codimension-one interface between two selected quantum-mechanical models is an invertible internal symmetry of its source model.
items.physical_scope: An exact finite-dimensional 0+1-dimensional transfer model with hbar=1 and zero Hamiltonians; it refutes only the stated universal identification of interfaces with internal symmetries.

references.title: Nils Carqueville, Lecture Notes on 2-Dimensional Defect TQFT
references.locator: §2.1, PDF pp. 5–8: interface data has a source region and target region, which need not be the same theory; the finite counterexample is proved locally.
